document_check.note: Franciotti R, Nardini D, Russo M, Onofrj M, Sensi SL. Comparison of Machine Learning-based Approaches to Predict the Conversion to Alzheimer's Disease from Mild Cognitive Impairment. Neuroscience 514 (2023) 143-152. ADNI MCI, RF/GB/XGB models by feature class. Matches the cited study (Franciotti et al. 2023).

cited_result: Ranking of feature classes for predicting conversion from MCI to AD within 36 months: sMRI-only models (n = 318) had the lowest accuracy (0.77 to 0.79) compared with models that include neuropsychological scores (0.81 to 0.83 alone, n = 587; up to 0.88 with sMRI, n = 318; up to 0.89 to 0.90 with AD biomarkers, n = 422).
tool_reason: The cited result ranks the discrimination (accuracy) of machine-learning prognostic models built on different predictor sets, which is model performance and so falls under PROBAST, with the PROBAST+AI considerations.

domains.rationale: The data source (ADNI longitudinal cohort) is appropriate, but no MCI eligibility criteria, selection numbers or handling of participants with under 36 months of follow-up are reported. Each feature class uses a different complete-data subset, and the sMRI subset is described as acquired on a single scanner type.

domains.rationale: Conversion to AD within 36 months is a standard horizon, but the paper gives no diagnostic criteria, no information on whether the diagnosing clinicians knew the predictors, and no information on whether cognitive or functional scores used as predictors (MMSE, CDR-SB, FAQ, ADAS-Cog) entered the diagnosis. That matters for the cited comparison, because incorporation of scores into the outcome would favour score-carrying models over sMRI-only models.

domains.rationale: Events per class are not reported and the test sets are small (15% of 318 is about 48 participants for sMRI). The analysis is complete-case with no stated missing-data handling, and performance rests on accuracy, PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity only, with no AUC and no calibration. There is a single random split, and hyperparameter tuning selected 'the best performance' with no statement that the test set was excluded. There is no cross-validation or external validation, and the 'Error' margins are undefined.

applicability.rationale: ADNI research volunteers, and the sMRI subset is from Philips 3 T scans. Generalisation to memory-clinic MCI is uncertain.
The outcome is conversion to AD dementia within 36 months, which matches the review's prognostic question.

overall: High risk of bias (PROBAST: participants unclear, predictors low, outcome unclear, analysis high)
overall_rationale: The analysis domain is high: no calibration or AUC, a single small random hold-out with unclear tuning isolation, unreported events, and complete-case subsets with no missing-data handling. Under PROBAST any high domain makes the overall rating high. The outcome definition is also unreported, and for this particular comparison (score-carrying versus sMRI-only) any incorporation of cognitive scores into the outcome would bias the ranking in the direction cited.
